subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Write the equation x + y + 2 = 0 in (a) slope-intercept form, (b) intercept form and (c) normal form.

mark_split.label: Divide and read cos α, sin α
Name α and write the normal form

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.158, chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 16(iv). **Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work** — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split follows the three parts the question names: two marks for each of the two easy forms, and four for the normal form, which is the only part with a sign condition in it — one for making the right side positive, two for dividing and reading cos α and sin α, and one for naming α. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C prints 3 long answer questions at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Every form was checked back against the original. The slope-intercept form y = −x − 2 rearranges to x + y + 2 = 0; the intercept form x/(−2) + y/(−2) = 1 multiplies by −2 to x + y = −2; and the normal form, with cos 225° = −1/√2 and sin 225° = −1/√2, reads −x/√2 − y/√2 = √2, which multiplies by −√2 back to x + y = −2. The value p = √2 also agrees with the direct perpendicular distance from the origin, |0 + 0 + 2|/√(1² + 1²) = 2/√2 = √2. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — name all three forms, and say what condition fixes the angle in the normal form.
formula_note: For the normal form, p must be positive — here moving the constant across leaves x+y=−2, a negative right side, so every term is negated before dividing by √(a²+b²). That flip makes cos α and sin α both negative, placing α in the third quadrant at 225°.

steps.label: Slope-intercept form
steps.margin_note: The first two marks. Quote y = mx + c, make y the subject, and then read off m and c separately.
lines: (a) Slope-intercept form is  y = mx + c

recall.must_convey: That making y the subject gives y = −x − 2, so m = −1 and c = −2.
accept: make y the subject to get y equals minus x minus two
slope intercept form is y equals m x plus c
the slope is minus one and c is minus two
y ni subject ga cheste minus x minus two vasthundi
m equals minus one and c equals minus two
heard_as: y equals m x plus c

steps.why: Slope-intercept form shows the slope and the y-intercept directly, so the work is to make y the subject.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as −y = x + 2 without dividing by −1.
steps.memory_tip: y = mx + c: make y the subject, then m is the number in front of x and c is what is left.

steps.label: Intercept form
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. Quote x/a + y/b = 1, move the constant to the right, and divide every term by it.

lines.text: (divide every term by −2, so that the right side is 1)

recall.must_convey: That dividing by −2 gives x/(−2) + y/(−2) = 1, so a = b = −2.
accept: move the constant right and divide by minus two
intercept form is x over a plus y over b equals one
a is minus two and b is minus two
constant tho divide chesthe intercept form vasthundi
x over minus two plus y over minus two equals one

steps.why: Intercept form must have 1 on the right-hand side, and dividing by the constant arranges that.
common_mistakes: Leaving −2 on the right instead of dividing to make it 1.
Dividing only one of the two terms by −2.
steps.memory_tip: x/a + y/b = 1 needs 1 on the right, so divide every term by the constant, sign included.

steps.label: Make the right side positive
steps.margin_note: One mark. Normal form carries the condition p > 0. Move the constant across and, if it is negative, change every sign.

steps.why: In normal form p is a perpendicular distance from the origin, so it must be positive, and that single condition is what fixes α.
common_mistakes: Dividing by √2 while the right side is still negative.
Changing the sign of only the constant term.
steps.memory_tip: p is a distance, so p > 0. If the constant is negative, change every sign at once.

steps.label: Divide and read cos α, sin α
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Divide every term by √((−1)² + (−1)²) = √2, then read cos α, sin α and p off the result in that order.

lines.text: (the coefficients of x and y are −1 and −1:
(compare with x cos α + y sin α = p)

recall.must_convey: That dividing by √2 gives cos α = −1/√2, sin α = −1/√2 and p = √2.
accept: divide by root two which is root of one plus one
cos alpha and sin alpha are both minus one over root two
p is root two
root a square plus b square tho divide cheyyali
divide every term by the root of the sum of the squares

steps.why: Dividing by the square root of the sum of the squares of the x and y coefficients makes them a cosine and a sine, because their squares then add to 1.
common_mistakes: Reading cos α and sin α as +1/√2 from the original x + y + 2 = 0.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √((−1)² + (−1)²) = √2 — the square root of the sum of the squares of the two coefficients.

steps.label: Name α and write the normal form
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Use the signs of cos α and sin α to name the quadrant, then write the finished normal form with the angle in it.
lines: cos α and sin α are both negative, so α lies

recall.must_convey: That both being negative puts α in the third quadrant, so α = 225°.
accept: both are negative so alpha is in the third quadrant
alpha is two hundred and twenty five degrees
x cos two twenty five plus y sin two twenty five equals root two
rendu negative so third quadrant, alpha two twenty five
one eighty plus forty five gives two twenty five

steps.why: The signs of cos α and sin α together name one quadrant, and that is what turns the pair of values into a single angle α.
common_mistakes: Naming α as 45° from the size of the numbers, ignoring the two minus signs.
Putting α in the second or fourth quadrant, where only one of the two is negative.
steps.memory_tip: Both cosine and sine negative means the third quadrant, so α = 180° + the related acute angle.
